perspective:
From Mason Hurley’s perspective, I know/experienced:

- I am an accountant at a small community center. Martha Moua is a personal care aide there; we are colleagues with a mainly work-related, not close, professional relationship.
- I reviewed financial reports and noticed discrepancies: healthcare expenses were unusually high and did not match usual spending patterns. This made me suspicious and anxious, leading me to suspect Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- I spoke with Martha about the report. I told her the numbers didn’t add up and pointed to the high healthcare expenses. I heard her say there might have been a misentry and that she would review and correct errors.
- After reviewing/clarifying with Martha, I concluded the discrepancies were a clerical error, not mismanagement. I felt relieved and embarrassed. I thanked Martha, apologized for my initial suspicion, and said I should have asked her first. I heard her say errors happen, it was okay, she understood I was being thorough, and we should double-check entries next time.
- I came to believe Martha is competent. I attributed the recurring errors to inadequate financial management systems, felt frustrated with the system, and felt empathy toward Martha.
- I discussed with Martha how to prevent future errors. I said the problem was not her management but the current system. I suggested a new, more robust financial system, said I would draft a proposal, and asked for her input. I heard her agree and offer to help.
- I drafted the new financial system proposal. I felt hopeful about its benefits but uncertain whether management would approve or implement it.
- I told Martha I had finished the draft and was unsure how management would receive it. I heard her encourage presenting with confidence, saying the benefits were clear. I planned a detailed presentation and asked Martha to help gather data. She agreed.
- I presented the proposal to management. I felt satisfied with my effort but physically and mentally exhausted, believing I had done everything possible to advocate for it. I told Martha the presentation went well and it was now up to management. I heard her praise my work, suggest taking time off, and offer help while away. I planned to take a few days off to recharge and reflect, hoping for good news.
- As of my last interaction, I do not yet know management’s decision.
